cities.name: Patan
cities.overview: A historic town in north Gujarat, once the capital of the Chaulukya (Solanki) kings, known for its stepwell and Patola silk weaving.

cities.name: Somnath
cities.overview: The temple town of Prabhas Patan on Gujarat's Saurashtra coast, next to the port of Veraval.

cities.name: Sasan Gir
cities.overview: The village at the edge of Gir forest in Junagadh district where lion safaris begin.

cities.name: Ahmedabad
cities.overview: Gujarat's largest city and India's first UNESCO World Heritage city, known for its old pols, mosques and textile history.
cities.history: Founded in 1411 by Sultan Ahmad Shah on the Sabarmati. It later grew rich on textiles, and Mahatma Gandhi based his independence work here from 1915.

cities.name: Vadodara
cities.overview: Old Baroda, capital of the Gaekwads, a cultured city with a palace, museums and Champaner nearby.
cities.history: The seat of the Gaekwad dynasty of the Marathas. Maharaja Sayajirao Gaekwad III turned it into a model of education and public works in the late 19th century.

cities.name: Bhuj
cities.overview: The old capital of Kutch, a small city rebuilt after the 2001 earthquake and a base for the Great Rann.

cities.name: Dwarka
cities.overview: A coastal temple town on the Okhamandal Peninsula, one of Hinduism's Char Dham and the legendary city of Krishna.

cities.name: Junagadh
cities.overview: A city at the foot of Girnar, with an old fort and ornate Nawabi tombs.

cities.name: Gandhinagar
cities.overview: Gujarat's planned capital, 23 km from Ahmedabad.

cities.name: Porbandar
cities.overview: A coastal city and the birthplace of Mahatma Gandhi.

cities.name: Bhavnagar
cities.overview: A Saurashtra port city, the base for Palitana and Velavadar.

cities.name: Mehsana
cities.overview: A north Gujarat city close to the Sun Temple at Modhera.

cities.name: Saputara
cities.overview: Gujarat's only real hill station, in the Dang forests of the Western Ghats.

cities.name: Palanpur
cities.overview: A north Gujarat town near the goddess shrine of Ambaji and the Polo Forest.

places.name: Rani ki Vav
places.shortDescription: An 11th-century stepwell in Patan, carved with hundreds of sculptures and pictured on the ₹100 note.
places.description: Rani ki Vav, the Queen's Stepwell, descends seven storeys into the ground as an inverted temple honouring water. Its walls carry more than 500 principal sculptures, many showing the avatars of Vishnu, apsaras and scenes of daily life, all remarkably crisp because the well lay buried under silt for centuries. The best light falls in the morning. While in Patan, visit a Patola weaving family, whose double-ikat silk takes months to make.
places.history: The stepwell was built around 1063 CE in memory of the Chaulukya king Bhima I, traditionally credited to his widowed queen Udayamati. It was excavated by the Archaeological Survey of India in the 1980s and inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2014.
places.bestTimeNote: October to March. Avoid the midday heat in summer.

entryFee.note: ASI World Heritage rates (slightly less online); verify before your visit.

sources.title: Rani-ki-Vav (the Queen's Stepwell) at Patan – UNESCO

places.name: Somnath Temple
places.shortDescription: The first of the twelve Jyotirlinga shrines of Shiva, rebuilt many times on the Arabian Sea shore.
places.description: The Somnath Temple stands right on the shore at Prabhas Patan, its Chaulukya-style spire facing the open sea. Tradition holds that there is no land between this shore and Antarctica, a claim marked on an arrow pillar in the courtyard. Evening aarti and the sound-and-light show tell the temple's long story. Phones and bags must be deposited before entering.
places.history: The temple was attacked and rebuilt many times, most famously after Mahmud of Ghazni's raid in 1026. The present temple was rebuilt after independence on the initiative of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel and consecrated in 1951.
places.bestTimeNote: October to March. Mahashivratri and the Kartik Purnima fair are the busiest days.

entryFee.note: Free entry; the sound-and-light show is ticketed.

location.address: Somnath Mandir Road, Prabhas Patan, Gir Somnath district, Gujarat 362268

places.name: Gir National Park
places.shortDescription: Dry deciduous forest that is the last wild home of the Asiatic lion.
places.description: Gir's teak and thorn forest is the only place in the world where Asiatic lions live in the wild, alongside leopards, spotted deer, sambar, nilgai and marsh crocodiles. Jeep safaris leave from Sasan Gir and must be booked online in advance, as permits sell out. The Maldhari herders who live inside the forest share it with the lions. The Devalia Safari Park nearby offers a shorter, fenced drive if permits for Gir are full.
places.history: Gir was protected by the Nawabs of Junagadh when lions were close to extinction in the early 20th century. It was declared a sanctuary in 1965, and the lion population has grown steadily since.
places.bestTimeNote: December to April. The park is closed from mid-June to mid-October.

entryFee.note: Safari permits are booked online on the Gujarat Forest Department site; prices vary by day and vehicle.

timings.hours: Three safari slots daily, early morning to evening

places.name: Sabarmati Ashram
places.shortDescription: Mahatma Gandhi's home on the Sabarmati from 1917 to 1930, starting point of the Salt March.
places.description: A calm riverside compound of whitewashed cottages. Gandhi's simple room stays as he left it, and a Charles Correa museum tells the story of his life.
places.history: Gandhi started the 1930 Dandi Salt March from here.

places.name: Sidi Saiyyed Mosque
places.shortDescription: A small 1573 mosque in Ahmedabad, famous for its stone lattice of an intertwined tree.
places.description: The carved Tree of Life window has become the emblem of the city. The rest of the mosque is simple, which puts all the attention on the screens.
places.history: Built by Sidi Sayyad, a Habshi nobleman, in 1572-73.

places.name: Adalaj Stepwell
places.shortDescription: A five-storey carved stepwell near Gandhinagar, built in 1498, cool even in summer.
places.description: Stairs drop through galleries of fine carved stone, to a deep well below. The light from the openings falls in shafts, so try to go around midday.
places.history: Built in 1498 in memory of Rana Veer Singh of the Vaghela dynasty, by his queen Rudabai.

places.name: Kankaria Lake
places.shortDescription: The largest lake in Ahmedabad, with a lakefront of rides, a zoo, a toy train and food stalls.
places.description: A circular lake with a walkway, a zoo and a balloon ride. It's where the city comes out on evenings and during the annual Kankaria Carnival.

places.name: Jama Masjid, Ahmedabad
places.shortDescription: A grand Friday mosque from 1424 in old Ahmedabad, with a forest of 260 pillars.
places.description: A huge sandstone courtyard opens from the noisy bazaar, and the prayer hall is held up by a maze of pillars. Hindu and Jain motifs show the way local styles blended.
places.history: Built in 1424 during the reign of Ahmad Shah I.

places.name: Hutheesing Jain Temple
places.shortDescription: A white marble Jain temple built in 1848, with detailed carving and a tall tower of fame.
places.description: A serene, richly carved marble temple built by a local merchant family. The Manastambha pillar outside is modelled on Chittor's Tower of Fame.
places.history: Built in 1848 by the Hutheesing family.

places.name: Calico Museum of Textiles
places.shortDescription: One of the finest textile collections in the world, in a Sarabhai family haveli.
places.description: A superb collection of Mughal-era tents, shawls, brocades and religious textiles, in wooden buildings. Entry is by guided tour only, so book ahead.
places.history: Managed by the Sarabhai Foundation.

places.name: Sarkhej Roza
places.shortDescription: A Sufi mosque and tomb complex 7 km south-west of Ahmedabad, built around a large tank.
places.description: A calm complex of tombs, a mosque and pavilions around a stepped lake. Le Corbusier compared it to the Acropolis.

places.name: Swaminarayan Akshardham
places.shortDescription: A big pink sandstone temple in Gandhinagar, with exhibitions and a water and light show.
places.description: Carved sandstone, spacious gardens and exhibitions on Swaminarayan's life, along with an evening water show. Phones aren't allowed inside.

places.name: Nal Sarovar
places.shortDescription: A 120 sq km shallow lake sanctuary 64 km west of Ahmedabad, with flamingos and pelicans in winter.
places.description: Boatmen pole you out across the shallow lake to see huge flocks of waterbirds in winter. Go at dawn for the best views.

places.name: Lothal
places.shortDescription: A site of the Indus Valley Civilisation in the Bhal region, with one of the world's oldest docks.
places.description: Low brick walls trace streets, houses, drains and a big dock in the flat Gujarat plain. The small museum displays beads, seals and pots.
places.history: One of the southernmost sites of the Indus Valley Civilisation.

places.name: Lakshmi Vilas Palace
places.shortDescription: A huge Indo-Saracenic palace from 1890, said to be four times the size of Buckingham Palace.
places.description: A vast palace on large grounds, with stained glass, mosaic floors and a Raja Ravi Varma collection. The royal family still lives there.
places.history: Commissioned in 1878 by Sayajirao Gaekwad III, and completed in 1890.

places.name: Champaner-Pavagadh
places.shortDescription: A UNESCO site near Vadodara, with a hill fort, Sultanate mosques and a hilltop temple.
places.description: Mosques and ruined city walls stand in the forest below Pavagadh hill, and a ropeway takes pilgrims to the Kalika Mata Temple on top.
places.history: Founded by Vanraj Chavda. Mahmud Begada captured it in 1484 and made it his capital.

places.name: Statue of Unity
places.shortDescription: The world's tallest statue at 182 m, of Sardar Patel, on the Narmada near Kevadia.
places.description: A viewing gallery in the chest offers a view over the Sardar Sarovar Dam. Around it are a flower valley, a safari park and other attractions.
places.history: Unveiled in 2018, in honour of independent India's first deputy prime minister.

places.name: Polo Forest
places.shortDescription: A dry forest at the foot of the Aravallis, with old Jain and Shiva temples hidden in the trees.
places.description: Ruined temples of the 15th century stand among trees and rivers near Vijaynagar. It's at its best after the monsoon, when it's green.

places.name: Ambaji Temple
places.shortDescription: A major goddess temple in Banaskantha, with no idol: a sacred yantra is worshipped instead.
places.description: One of Gujarat's busiest temples. Gabbar Hill nearby has a ropeway, and the Bhadarvi Poonam fair each September draws huge crowds.

places.name: Sun Temple, Modhera
places.shortDescription: A carved 11th-century Surya temple on the Pushpavati river, with a stepped tank in front.
places.description: Pillared halls and a deep stepped tank, with sunlight once lined up to reach the sanctum. Carvings of the 12 Adityas line the walls.
places.history: Built by Bhima I of the Chaulukya dynasty in the early 11th century.

places.name: Great Rann of Kutch
places.shortDescription: A vast white salt desert in Kutch, among the largest in the world, stunning under a full moon.
places.description: A flat white salt plain spreading to the horizon, with the Rann Utsav tent city at Dhordo each winter. Permits are needed, and they can be bought on the way there.
places.bestTimeNote: The salt is only dry enough to walk on from about November to February.

places.name: Aina Mahal
places.shortDescription: An 18th-century mirror palace in Bhuj, built by a craftsman who trained in Europe.
places.description: A small palace of mirror work, Delft tiles and gold, partly restored after the earthquake of 2001.
places.history: Built around 1750 by Rao Lakhpatji of Kutch State and his master craftsman, Ram Singh Malam.

places.name: Prag Mahal
places.shortDescription: A 19th-century Italian Gothic palace in Bhuj, with a clock tower looking over the town.
places.description: An unusual Gothic palace in Kutch, with Italian marble and a clock tower that you can climb, though it's visibly damaged by the earthquake.

places.name: Dholavira
places.shortDescription: A UNESCO Indus Valley city on Khadir island in the Rann, famous for its water system.
places.description: A stone city of reservoirs, with an ancient signboard in Indus script. It's a long but rewarding drive, across the white Rann.
places.history: Added to the UNESCO World Heritage list in 2021.

places.name: Vijaya Vilas Palace
places.shortDescription: The Maharao of Kutch's summer palace on the beach at Mandvi, with a private beach.
places.description: A red stone palace in a garden of fruit trees, with a big terrace looking out on the beach. Mandvi's old shipyard is nearby.

places.name: Indian Wild Ass Sanctuary
places.shortDescription: A 4,954 sq km reserve in the Little Rann of Kutch, the last home of the Indian wild ass.
places.description: Jeeps cross the cracked salt flats to find herds of wild ass, along with flamingos and desert foxes. Dasada is the usual base.

places.name: Dwarkadhish Temple
places.shortDescription: The Jagat Mandir of Krishna in Dwarka, a tall carved temple by the Gomti river.
places.description: A five-storey temple with a soaring tower, topped with a flag that's changed several times a day. The steps down to the Gomti ghat are a good place to stop.

places.name: Bet Dwarka
places.shortDescription: An island in the Gulf of Kutch, off Okha, with a Krishna temple, and now reached by a bridge.
places.description: Traditionally thought of as Krishna's home. Visitors come for the temple, though the white sands and dolphins are worth a look.

places.name: Nageshwar Jyotirlinga
places.shortDescription: One of the twelve Jyotirlinga temples of Shiva, near Dwarka, with a tall Shiva statue.
places.description: A modest shrine with a large statue of Shiva out in the open, a usual stop on the road between Dwarka and Bet Dwarka.

places.name: Marine National Park
places.shortDescription: India's first marine park, in the Gulf of Kutch, with corals, sea stars and dolphins.
places.description: At low tide, you can walk on the reef at Narara with a guide, past sea stars, octopus and coral. Go during low tide and bring old shoes.
places.history: A marine sanctuary was declared in 1980 from Okha to Jodiya.

sources.title: Marine National Park, Gulf of Kutch – Wikipedia

places.name: Kirti Mandir
places.shortDescription: The memorial museum at Mahatma Gandhi's birthplace in Porbandar, with his childhood home next door.
places.description: A museum in a small coastal city, with photographs and items of Mahatma and Kasturba Gandhi. The old house where he was born is right next door.

places.name: Uparkot Fort
places.shortDescription: An ancient fort in Junagadh, with cave monasteries and two stepwells cut into the rock.
places.description: A fort thought to be over 2,000 years old, with Buddhist caves, Adi Kadi Vav and Navghan Kuvo, a deep, spiral stepwell.

places.name: Mahabat Maqbara
places.shortDescription: A dazzling 1892 mausoleum in Junagadh, with silver doors and spiral-staircase minarets.
places.description: A wild mix of Islamic, Gothic and Indian styles. Its onion domes and spiralling minarets make it one of Gujarat's most photographed buildings.
places.history: Completed in 1892 for Mahabat Khan II, Nawab of Junagadh.

places.name: Girnar
places.shortDescription: A sacred mountain at Junagadh, with Jain and Hindu temples, reached by steps or a ropeway.
places.description: Thousands of steps climb the volcanic hill past Jain temples to Hindu shrines at the top. A ropeway now takes you most of the way up.
places.history: Sacred to Jains as the place where Neminath attained nirvana.

places.name: Palitana Temples
places.shortDescription: Hundreds of Jain marble temples on Shatrunjaya hill, reached by a long climb of stone steps.
places.description: A mountain of temples, and the most sacred Jain site in Gujarat. Pilgrims walk barefoot up the steps at dawn, and no one is allowed to stay on the hill at night.

places.name: Blackbuck National Park
places.shortDescription: A grassland reserve near Bhavnagar, with large herds of blackbuck and harriers in winter.
places.description: Golden grassland on the Gulf of Khambhat, where blackbuck leap in large numbers. It's among the largest winter roosts of harriers in the world.
places.history: Established in 1976 in the Bhal region.

places.name: Saputara Lake
places.shortDescription: Gujarat's main hill station, in the Dang forests, with a lake, gardens and sunset point.
places.description: A green escape in Gujarat's dry summer, with boating, a ropeway and the Gira Waterfalls nearby. The monsoon festival is its busiest time.
